tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent (patching failed, why it failed, how to fix it), explicitly lists many trigger contexts (failed/timed-out/cancelled runs, specific error types like disk full, GPG, proxy, TLS, WSUS, CBS errors, Linux and Windows), and explicitly pushes for broad application ('load it first even when the cause looks obvious or the user only pastes an error message'). It is a dense but still a single cohesive paragraph focused on scope, not implementation mechanics.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when an EC2 patch run has failed, or a user asks why patching failed or how to fix it, and load it first even when the cause looks obvious or the user only pastes an error message or code.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body skips general explanations of EC2, SSM, or patching concepts and goes straight into project-specific procedures: required context fields, gates, SOP selection rules, and command execution rules. It is dense but each piece is actionable and domain-specific, not generic background.
tests.evidence:
Collect these before any other step and use them on every call:
- account_id: the member account that owns the instance.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large reference tables (error codes, SOP content, metric thresholds) are embedded in the body. SOP details, execution guide specifics, and templates all live in references/ and are only linked, not duplicated inline.
tests.evidence: Open only the SOP files the [SOP index](references/sop-index.md) shortlisted in Step 6.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ (sop-index.md, execution-guide.md, remediation-plan-template.md, command-plan-template.md, and each SOP file) is linked with markdown link syntax in the body, including the full SOP file listing table.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The Files table explicitly ties each reference file to a workflow step and condition (e.g. 'Step 6, first', 'Steps 10 and 12', 'Step 8'), clearly indicating when to load each.
tests.evidence: [references/execution-guide.md](references/execution-guide.md) | Steps 10 and 12: the exact `use_aws` calls for running an SOP step and re-running a patch.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference file links use relative paths from the skill root (references/...) with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (running commands verbatim, gate checks, retry limits) are prescriptive and exact, while diagnostic reasoning (finding root cause, matching SOP) explains WHY and gives the agent judgment latitude, appropriately matching rigor to fragility.
tests.evidence: Only run code blocks from `references/sops/`, verbatim, one step per command. ... Read the whole error output and identify the exact failure.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present competing tools as a menu; it is prescriptive about which SOP to pick based on matching criteria rather than offering several equally valid approaches.
tests.evidence: Does not apply: the skill routes to a single matched SOP via defined matching criteria rather than offering multiple equal tool options.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow (Steps 1-12) is a fully generalizable procedure applicable to any failed patch run across many platforms/distributions, not a one-off instance-specific declaration.
tests.evidence: Copy this checklist and work through it in order. Steps 1-8 run in every mode; steps 9-12 run only in chat, with operator approval.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: A 'Common pitfalls' section is present with concrete, non-obvious corrections specific to this domain (e.g., treating the SSM lock as the cause, editing SOP commands).
tests.evidence: | Treating "lock" as the cause | SSM always takes a lock. Find the real failure. |

tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-validation step before presenting output, checking the plan for verbatim command copying, no placeholders, and format correctness.
